purpose: HPE Aruba Networking DevHub landing, SDK, package, sample, and developer guidance pages for RAG discovery.
notes: Crawled by ingestion/scrape_devhub.py. The manifest previously pointed at scrape.py, which hardcodes the developer_docs output directory and its own seeds, so it never produced a DevHub corpus. DevHub publishes no sitemap, so pages are found by breadth-first crawl; content is in #content and query strings are dropped because the catalog filters re-render the same page. Do not commit scraped content; source URLs are preserved in each file.

purpose: New Central developer and API how-to pages from the Aruba developer portal.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape.py and scrape_cnac_spec.py, then rebuild data/docs.lance and data/specs.sqlite.

purpose: General HPE Aruba technical documentation used by docs RAG retrieval.
notes: Keep generated markdown or HTML under the git-ignored source folder with source URL comments. The doc-portal landing page is a JS doc-browser that exposes no usable book index, and only VSG serves a sitemap.xml, so the WebHelp books are walked breadth-first per book by ingestion/scrape_techdocs_books.py: CLI-Bank (the AOS-10/CoP/ClearPass/SD-Branch CLI command reference), central-on-premises, AOS-Switch-RN and AirWave. hpe-central is handled separately by ingestion/scrape_hpe_central_pw.py under the techdocs_html source. The four books above are the complete set of live WebHelp books: every ArubaDocPortal product category page (including its client-side ?tab=N panes) was enumerated and the only other in-site book root it reaches is /techdocs/Archived/, which holds superseded product versions and is deliberately excluded. /techdocs/new-central/ is only an alias that redirects into hpe-central.

purpose: Network access control, MAC registration, visitor, MPSK, DPP, and certificate reference material.
notes: Slugs discovered from the public new-central-config reference index, filtered to the NAC/AAA/security surface (261 pages), then the <article> prose is extracted with pandoc (icons/scripts stripped) at a 1.5s per-request delay. Replaces ingestion/scrape_reference.py, which read a URL list from /tmp files that no longer exist and wrote to ingestion/markdown/ instead of this output_dir — so nac_docs was silently never populated. Pair prose refreshes with the CNAC OpenAPI extraction when NAC API pages change.

purpose: Validated Solution Guide pages and design guidance used by architecture and workflow RAG answers.
notes: Build the URL list with ingestion/discover_vsg_urls.py (reads the guide's sitemap), then refresh with ingestion/scrape_vsg.py. Do not seed from /techdocs/VSG/docs/: Apache returns 403 for that directory listing even though the pages under it serve normally. Requires Playwright with headless=False for Akamai, plus pandoc for HTML->markdown. Japanese translations are excluded by default.

purpose: HPE Aruba Networking Central product documentation, feature pages, workflows, and UI terminology.
notes: The techdocs book moved from new-central to hpe-central and is now published as Oxygen WebHelp (GUID-*.html topics). Akamai 403s direct sub-resource requests, so ingestion/scrape_hpe_central_pw.py BFS-crawls topic pages with paced Playwright navigation instead of reading the site's file list. The book is larger than the default --max-pages bound, so re-run with --skip-existing until it reports no new pages (about 2000 topics).

purpose: AOS-CX per-switch-platform feature/release support matrix and AOS10 (AP/gateway) feature/release matrix, for RAG answers about hardware/software feature support.
notes: The page itself (https://feature-navigator.arubanetworking.hpe.com/wired and /aos10) is a client-rendered Next.js app with no data in its initial HTML, but its compiled JS bundles call a small unauthenticated public JSON API that returns the real comparison data directly: /api/productInfo lists every AOS-CX switch platform with its supported release list, /api/switchReleaseCompatibility?productId=&productReleaseNames=&licenses=1,2,3 returns that platform's full feature Yes/No matrix for the requested releases, and /api/releases + /api/releaseCompatibility?ids=&releases= do the same for the shared AOS10 (AP/gateway/Mobility Controller) image. Only the latest AOS-CX release is captured per switch platform (current-state snapshot); the AOS10 side keeps every published release since the response stays small and shows which release introduced a feature. 5 of the 25 productInfo entries (5400R, 3810, 2930F/M, 2540, 2530) are legacy ProVision/AOS-S platforms whose supportedReleases use AOS-S version strings (e.g. YA/YB.16.08.0001), not real AOS-CX releases, so they are deliberately skipped rather than queried; CX 4100i's supportedReleases also contains a literal "#REF!" Excel artifact that is filtered out before selecting its latest real release.

purpose: Authoritative OpenAPI specs for exact endpoint, schema, field, and enum lookup.
notes: JSON specs are parsed into docs chunks and data/specs.sqlite; include CNAC via ingestion/scrape_cnac_spec.py and the pinned official Mist snapshot via ingestion/fetch_mist_openapi.py. ingestion/fetch_manifest_specs.py fetches the 30 registries named in openapi_registry_manifest.json by id. Coverage against the portal was then checked end to end: enumerating the new-central and new-central-config api-next sidebars yields 32 specs holding 2725 operations, of which 2713 were already on disk under registry-suffixed names, so ingestion/fetch_central_apinext_specs.py adds only wholly-new specs and reports the rest as drift. The portal no longer serves the per-slug specs (aaa-profile.json and friends) that the committed Central manifest was built from; both scrape_openapi.py and the api-next sidebar now return consolidated per-area documents, so those 243 files cannot be re-fetched.

purpose: AOS 10 techdocs books for Wi-Fi design, location services, private 5G, and AOS operations.
notes: Discover URLs with ingestion/discover_aos_urls.py and refresh with ingestion/scrape_aos_pw.py.

purpose: Official HPE Aruba Networking CSAF security advisories across hardware, software, cloud, NAC, SD-WAN, and management products.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape_security_lifecycle.py. The incremental changes.csv feed covers the complete official Aruba advisory archive and preserves advisory IDs, CVEs, severity, affected products, fixed versions, and remediation text.

purpose: Official HPE Networking end-of-sale, replacement-product, and support-lifecycle notices across all networking product categories.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape_security_lifecycle.py. The XML feed is the data source behind HPE's historical all-product End of Sale archive (no current Aruba-branded entries; nothing published after 2020); the official hardware PDF adds SKU-level dates and replacements but is a static 2020-05-06 snapshot. HPE does not publish a current crawlable index for every individual modern notice, so answers must cite the notice date and avoid implying the archive is exhaustive beyond its published entries. See docs/source-lifecycle-coverage.md and ingestion.scrape_security_lifecycle.HPE_ARUBA_CURRENT_LIFECYCLE_COVERAGE_GAP for the full evidenced coverage-gap boundary for current Aruba-branded lifecycle notices.

purpose: Official Juniper lifecycle milestone tables for the Mist and Apstra product families exposed by hpe-networking-mcp's optional backends.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape_security_lifecycle.py. Juniper publishes these as server-rendered lifecycle tables rather than a public structured feed. discover_juniper_lifecycle_urls() additionally re-derives this same reviewed set (and any future officially-added Mist/Apstra page) from the official EOL index nav at the last seed_urls entry, deduplicated by absolute URL.

purpose: Official Juniper security bulletins for the Mist and Apstra product families exposed by hpe-networking-mcp's optional backends.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape_security_lifecycle.py. discover_juniper_security_sitemaps() fetches and parses the official sitemap index above into its current topic-article child sitemap URLs (host/scheme/path validated, sitemap-topicarticle-*.xml only); discover_juniper_security_urls() then reads each child sitemap and filters to Mist/Apstra Security Bulletin articles. Playwright renders the Salesforce article body because plain HTTP receives only the application shell.

purpose: Juniper support-portal knowledge articles for Mist and Apstra: troubleshooting, licensing, and configuration guidance.
notes: Covers the Mist/Apstra articles that scrape_security_lifecycle.py leaves behind: it keeps only the formal Security Bulletins, which are a tiny fraction of the in-scope articles. The portal is a Salesforce Lightning app whose raw HTML holds no article text, so pages must be rendered with Playwright (headless=False).

purpose: Juniper Mist-family documentation (wireless, wired, WAN, access assurance, Juniper Validated Designs, and the Mist/Marvis-based data center + routing assurance products) for fuzzy howto/concept RAG search.
notes: URLs discovered from juniper.net's public sitemap (discover_mist_docs_urls.py matches 5 path prefixes: mist, jvd, hpe-mist-networking-data-center-assurance, juniper-data-center-assurance, juniper-routing-assurance — all Mist/Marvis-family products; excludes Junos core-OS and unrelated Juniper product lines as out of scope), then scraped via plain urllib + pandoc (server-rendered DITA HTML, no Playwright needed) with a 4-worker pool and a 0.4s per-request delay to avoid rate-limiting/IP bans. 2,014 URLs scraped as of the last full run (2,011 OK, 3 stale sitemap 404s). Excludes /software/mist/api/ (JS widget) — see mist_openapi_spec in openapi_specs' extra_scripts for the real API spec.

purpose: OpenAPI specs for the non-Central Aruba developer-portal products: AOS-CX, AOS-8, Central 2.x, ClearPass, UXI, Fabric Composer, and EdgeConnect Orchestrator.
notes: These seven portal sections run ReadMe's api-next v2 API, so they carry no oasPublicUrl pointer for scrape_openapi.py to parse, and the admin /apis listing is 403 for anonymous callers. The public per-page reference endpoint embeds the whole OpenAPI document under data.api.schema, so one fetch per sidebar category recovers every spec. Kept separate from openapi_specs (Central-only) so the generated Central client and manifest are unaffected; these are embedded for semantic search rather than added to the exact SQLite spec index. Discovery manifest: ingestion/product_specs_manifest.json.

purpose: Official Juniper EX-series switch and Mist-family access-point hardware datasheet specifications (port density, throughput, PoE, Wi-Fi standard, radios, mounting) for exact hardware-spec RAG lookup.
notes: URLs are filtered directly out of juniper.net's flat product sitemap (2,130 <loc> entries; distinct from the documentation sitemap discover_mist_docs_urls.py reads) rather than cached to a seed file, because the whole corpus is ~50 pages fetched in well under a minute — not the multi-hour crawl that justifies mist_docs_urls.json. EX-series .../specs.html pages extract div.cmp-specifications (a stable Adobe Experience Manager component verified across EX2300-EX9250); AP .../*-datasheet.html pages have no such wrapper but always carry exactly 5 <table> elements with the real spec content, rendered generically (a table whose first row has >2 cells becomes a markdown comparison table, otherwise label/value bullets). Aruba/HPE-branded hardware pages (arubanetworks.com, arubanetworking.hpe.com, www.hpe.com) were probed from this environment and every one returned an Akamai 403 or a hard HTTP/2 stream reset — including via a genuine headless-Chromium Playwright request — so this source is Juniper-only by evidenced necessity, not by choice; Aruba CX/AP exact specs are served instead by hpe_networking_mcp.pipeline.clients.hardware_specs, which ask_docs consults before RAG.
